title: Franchise Architect: Football
statusLine: Franchise Architect: Football is free to play in early access. It is complete enough to run a franchise for decades, and it changes often; every change is dated in the changelog.
heroSubline: No account, no install, no server. It runs in your browser.
privacyLine: Your league is saved in this browser. Nothing leaves it unless you turn on anonymous Community Stats or choose GitHub Gist sync.
intelligenceLine: No AI services and no paid APIs. Every rival, every Advisor call and every headline is worked out by the game's own rules from your league's data.

heroImage.alt: The franchise Desk: your club, its competitive window and needs, cap space, the press room and the controls to advance the season
heroImage.title: The Desk

facts.label: Platform
facts.value: Web browser on desktop, tablet and phone

facts.label: Price
facts.value: Free. Nothing to buy inside the game.

facts.label: Accounts
facts.value: None. No account, no install, no server. Saves live in the browser, with optional export and GitHub Gist sync.

facts.label: League
facts.value: 32 clubs and 31 rival front offices, for as many seasons as you keep playing

facts.label: AI
facts.value: No AI services. Rivals, the Advisor and the news are computed by the game's own rules.

features.title: A Front Office Advisor that shows its work
features.teaser: Each week it argues one call, with the numbers behind it, and keeps score when you overrule it.
features.description: Each week the Advisor on your Desk argues for one call from your briefing and shows the cap, roster and results figures it is reading. You can take the advice or ignore it. The Advisor keeps score of how often you went against it and what happened next. Its reasoning runs on the game's own rules and your league's data. It uses no AI service, and nothing is sent anywhere.

image.alt: The First Season Contract objectives and the Front Office Advisor arguing one call, with the figures behind it

features.title: A First Season Contract
features.teaser: Five objectives every first-year general manager is judged on.
features.description: A new franchise opens with five objectives: sign a free agent, set a depth chart yourself, work the trade desk, reach the owner's win target, and carry a legal cap into the offseason. Each one is ticked off from what you actually do. At the season review the contract closes with the owner's verdict.

features.title: Thirty-one front offices that remember you
features.teaser: Every rival general manager has a way of valuing players and a memory of your last deal.
features.description: Every rival club is run by a general manager with an archetype. A win-now club accepts a wider price than a rebuilding one. A player at their real need carries a premium and a surplus position a discount, and the offer tells you which applied. Rivals remember the deals you have done together, including the ones they are still annoyed about, and they call on draft day to buy your pick.

image.alt: A rival general manager's trade offer, with what they want and why

features.title: A league that trades around you
features.teaser: Rival clubs trade with each other under the same roster, cap and deadline rules you do.
features.description: Rival clubs trade with each other during the season, under the same roster, cap and deadline rules that govern your deals. Their moves are reported in League News, so the league changes even when you hold your own roster steady.

features.title: An owner you answer to
features.teaser: Facilities cost real money and upkeep, ticket prices meet a market, and the owner's patience runs out.
features.description: The Boardroom holds your owner, your facilities, your coaching staff and your franchise identity. Facilities are building projects paid from the owner's cash, and every wing you own costs upkeep each year. Ticket prices answer to a market that punishes greed. You hire from a coaching market whose staff age and move on. The owner's patience is shown as a meter, and it can run out.

image.alt: The Boardroom: the owner's mandate and finances, facilities, and the head coach market

features.title: A cap that binds
features.teaser: Extensions, restructures, franchise tags and an offseason where contracts really expire.
features.description: Every contract sits under a salary cap that applies from the first snap: extensions, restructures, franchise tags and cap casualties, with a multi-year cap view to plan against. Contracts expire, rivals fight to re-sign their own stars, and free agency resolves in bidding waves that wait for your moves.

image.alt: The Contracts screen: cap space, expiring deals and franchise-tag candidates

features.title: Scouts give you a read, not the answer
features.teaser: Draft prospects arrive in scouting fog. Spend scouting points to see more clearly.
features.description: Draft prospects arrive in scouting fog. Your board shows your scouts' estimate of each prospect's overall and potential, and the scouting points you spend move that estimate closer to the truth. Lock your board, then run the draft from the war room while rivals call to trade up.

features.title: Set the plan, then watch it play out
features.teaser: A weekly tactical plan that changes how your team plays, and Sim-Watch replays of the key plays.
features.description: Before kickoff you choose the week's tactical focus, and it changes how your team plays. Sim-Watch replays a game's key plays as a broadcast, with play-by-play, a speed control and a final reel. The simulation runs in the background on browsers that support it, so the game stays responsive while a season simulates.

features.title: The league writes its own history
features.teaser: Awards, records, a Dynasty timeline and a Hall of Fame with an induction ceremony.
features.description: Season awards, league and franchise records, retired numbers, a Dynasty timeline, and a Hall of Fame with a ballot and an induction ceremony. Beat reporters, press conferences and League News remember what happened, so your franchise builds a history it can tell back to you.

features.title: Moments worth sharing
features.teaser: Turn trophies, picks and whole seasons into shareable cards.
features.description: Trophies, the season epilogue, the development report and a first-round pick can be saved as image cards. A League Story Card sums up a season, and a Dynasty Timeline sums up a whole run.

features.title: Challenge codes
features.teaser: Send a friend the same league, from the same seed.
features.description: Every league can produce a challenge code. A friend who pastes it on the start page gets the same league from the same starting point, so you can run the same franchise and compare.

features.title: Measured realism
features.teaser: Elite talent is held to a ceiling drawn from real football honors, and the limits are published.
features.description: The share of elite players is held to a ceiling based on how many players real football honors each season. Season statistics are kept within real-world ranges, and the methodology page explains where the comparison stops working.

features.title: A career, not a save file
features.teaser: Six GM legacy tiers, from Young Gun to Immortal, earned from results.
features.description: Your record follows you across every franchise in this browser through six legacy tiers, from Young Gun to Immortal. Tiers are earned only from results the game can verify you produced.

features.title: Commissioner mode
features.teaser: Up to four general managers share one league on the same device.
features.description: Create a commissioner lobby and give each general manager a club. Everyone stages their moves for the week, then the commissioner advances it. Lobbies are stored in this browser, so this is a shared-device mode. There is no online multiplayer.

features.title: Saves that protect themselves
features.teaser: Local saves, rolling backups, a rewind ledger, exports and optional Gist sync.
features.description: Your league saves in this browser, with rolling automatic backups and rewind points for recent major decisions. You can export a save file at any time, or sync it to a GitHub Gist with a token you supply. That token is sent only to GitHub and is kept only for the current tab.

features.title: It is your franchise
features.teaser: Name the team, set the city, choose the colors and the era.
features.description: Name the team, set the city, choose the colors, the era and the ruleset. Your club's crest and identity carry through the whole game.

features.title: Community Stats, if you want them
features.teaser: An optional, anonymous look at what other general managers are doing.
features.description: Community Stats is off until you turn it on. When it is on, the game shares anonymous choices and results, never your save, names or notes. A trend stays hidden until enough players are included for it to mean anything.
